title: Flight deck log: course events
body:
U.S.S. APOLLO-MEME  /  FLIGHT DECK  /  AUTOMATED LOG

15-OCT-2011 03:14:22 UTC  Cabin thermostat adjustment requested at flight interface. Input source: manual.
15-OCT-2011 03:14:23 UTC  WARNING: control mapped to PROPULSION, not CABIN CLIMATE. Hyper-drive toggle state: ENGAGED.
15-OCT-2011 03:14:24 UTC  Navigation lock applied. Vector: outbound, away from lunar transfer corridor.
15-OCT-2011 03:14:31 UTC  Operator override attempted. Result: REJECTED. Trajectory cannot be corrected under current configuration.

No further entries from this station.

[Technician's note, handwritten on the printout]  Someone label that switch. Please. - {callsign:pilot}

author: commander
title: Note from the commander's footlocker
body:
Crew,

I have drawn up the watch rota. Read it. Memorise it. Nobody leaves a post without telling me, and nobody, NOBODY, gives up an inch of this ship.

We are going home. That is not a hope, it is an order.

- {name:commander}

author: scout
title: Scrawled journal page
body:
DAY ??? (lost count)

barked at the telemetry AGAIN. it did not bark back. neither did the other one. the other one did something worse. it just looked at me.

going to run the east loop twice. fast is a plan. fast is ALWAYS a plan.

- {callsign:scout}

author: pilot
title: Sticky notes, flight deck handwriting
body:
TO DO
[x] Do not touch the heater toggle
[x] Label the heater toggle
[x] Label the OTHER toggle that is not the heater toggle
[ ] Apologise to {callsign:commander} (again)
[ ] Stop clicking things when it is quiet

If you are reading this: the sticky notes are not decoration. They are the only thing keeping me from clicking.

author: quartermaster
title: Quartermaster's inventory scrap
body:
Morale: low. Freeze-dried snacks: lower. Patience: not tracked, since the stock count ended at zero.

Only item still in surplus is optimism, and it is all {callsign:commander}'s.

Filed under: things that were fine until they weren't.

author: quartermaster
title: Supply manifest (partial)
body:

title: Engineering access: maintenance log
body:
ENGINEERING ACCESS CORRIDOR  /  MAINTENANCE

Coolant line 2 weeping at the junction. Steam vents venting on schedule, which is the only thing on schedule.

Engine core access remains SEALED under emergency protocol. Re-opening requires override credentials held by flight systems.

Hull sections upstream report intermittent pressure irregularity. Do not linger in the damaged corridor.
